a strike-slip zone can be modeled by a single fault and a ductility contrast between the fault plane and the surrounding rock.
the slip rate is controlled by the far-field strain and the depth of the shear zone, and that the vertical distribution of strain and stress is controlled by the vertical rheological profile.
a deep strike-slip fault can be considered as an effective dislocation in a linear viscous medium.

, for large vertical rheological variation, the deformation in the shear zone is distributed over half the vertical extent of a fault.
a thick ductile layer beneath the fault is required to generate a thick transition zone of distributed deformation.
